name: Wi-Fi
intro: A Wi-Fi QR code lets a phone camera join your network without typing the password: scan it and the device fills in the network name, security type and password automatically.
tips: Use WPA/WPA2/WPA3 unless the router genuinely only supports WEP or is open.
Passwords are case-sensitive — copy them exactly, including symbols.
For a guest network, tick "hidden" only if you actually disabled SSID broadcast.
Print it near the router or at reception; laminate it if it will get handled a lot.

faqs.q: Does the Wi-Fi QR code send my password anywhere?
faqs.a: No. The WIFI: string with your SSID and password is generated and encoded entirely in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

faqs.q: Will it work on both iPhone and Android?
faqs.a: Yes. Both the native camera apps (iOS 11+, Android 10+) and most third-party scanners understand the WIFI: format.

faqs.q: What if I change the Wi-Fi password later?
faqs.a: The old code will stop connecting — generate and print a new one. Because it is static, there is no way to update a printed code remotely.

name: vCard / contact card
h1: QR code for a vCard (contact card)
intro: A vCard QR code puts your name, phone, email and company into a contact card that a scan can save directly to the recipient's phone contacts — no app or manual typing required.
tips: Keep it to the essentials: name, phone, email, company. Long addresses make a denser, harder-to-scan code.
Test-scan on both iPhone and Android before printing business cards in bulk.
For a team, generate one vCard per person rather than a shared one, so caller ID and "who scanned" stay accurate.
Use error correction level Q or H if the card will be printed small (under 3cm).

faqs.q: What is the vCard format?
faqs.a: vCard 3.0 (RFC 2426) — the same standard address-book apps already use, so contacts import with the right fields instead of landing as one blob of text.

faqs.q: Can I include a photo?
faqs.a: Not in the QR code itself — embedding an image would make the code far too dense to scan reliably. Add the photo after import, or link to an online profile instead.

faqs.q: Does this replace a digital business card app?
faqs.a: It replaces the need for one for the core "save my contact" action — with no app, account or ongoing dependency on a third-party service.

name: WhatsApp
intro: A WhatsApp QR code opens a chat with your number pre-filled — and, optionally, a starter message already typed in — the moment someone scans it.
tips: Enter the number in full international format (e.g. +1 555 000 0000); the tool strips spaces and dashes automatically.
A short pre-filled message ("Hi, I found you via the QR code") makes it obvious why someone is messaging you.
This links to wa.me, WhatsApp's own click-to-chat service — not a third-party redirect, so it keeps working as long as WhatsApp does.
Test on a phone without WhatsApp installed too: it falls back to the WhatsApp web/download page.

faqs.q: Does this require WhatsApp Business?
faqs.a: No, it works with a regular personal WhatsApp number as well as WhatsApp Business.

faqs.q: Can people see my number just from the QR code image?
faqs.a: The number is inside the encoded link (wa.me/<number>), so yes — anyone can decode the image and read it, the same as with any WhatsApp click-to-chat link.

faqs.q: Can I change the pre-filled message later?
faqs.a: Not on an already-printed code; generate a new one. The message is only a suggestion — the person can edit it before sending.

name: Instagram profile
h1: QR code for your Instagram profile
intro: Point a QR code straight at your Instagram profile URL (instagram.com/yourhandle) so a scan opens the app — or the web profile — directly, with no extra taps.
tips: Use the full https://instagram.com/yourhandle URL, not just "@yourhandle".
This is a direct link, not a dynamic one: it keeps working for as long as your profile exists at that handle.
If you might rename your handle later, consider a link-in-bio page instead and point the QR at that — just know that adds a dependency on that service.
Add your logo to the code's centre (Style settings) to reinforce the brand at a glance.

faqs.q: Will scanning open the Instagram app or a browser?
faqs.a: On a phone with Instagram installed, most camera apps hand the link to the app directly; otherwise it opens the profile in a browser.

faqs.q: Does this QR code expire?
faqs.a: No — it is a direct link to your profile URL, generated and stored entirely in the code. It only stops working if you delete or rename that profile.

name: YouTube video or channel
h1: QR code for a YouTube video or channel
intro: Encode a YouTube video or channel URL so scanning jumps straight to your content — handy on posters, packaging or a presentation's closing slide.
tips: Use the full canonical URL (youtube.com/watch?v=… or youtube.com/@handle), not a shortened youtu.be link if you want the address itself printed alongside the code.
For a specific moment, add &t=90s to start playback partway through.
A larger code (at least 3×3cm printed) scans more reliably against motion-graphics backgrounds.
Test the scan from across a room if it will be shown on a screen or projector.

faqs.q: Does the QR code depend on YouTube staying up?
faqs.a: It depends only on the video or channel remaining at that URL — not on any third-party QR service. If YouTube ever removed the video, the code itself would still be valid, it would just lead nowhere.

faqs.q: Can I track how many people scanned it?
faqs.a: Not with a static code — there is no server in the loop to log scans. A dynamic/tracked code can do that, but then depends on that provider's subscription; see our static vs dynamic guide.

name: Google review link
h1: QR code to collect Google reviews
intro: Turn your Google "write a review" link into a QR code on a receipt, table tent or counter card, so customers can leave a review in a couple of taps.
tips: Get your review link from Google Business Profile → "Ask for reviews", or build one at g.page/r/<place-id>/review.
This is a direct Google URL, not a third-party redirect — it keeps working for as long as your Business Profile exists.
Place the code somewhere a satisfied customer naturally pauses: at checkout, on the receipt, or on the table.
Pair it with a one-line prompt ("Enjoyed your visit? Scan to leave a review") — a code with no context gets ignored.

faqs.q: Is it against Google's policy to ask for reviews this way?
faqs.a: Asking customers to leave a review is allowed; offering money, discounts or gifts in exchange for a review, or filtering who gets asked based on expected rating, is not.

faqs.q: Where do I find my exact review link?
faqs.a: In Google Business Profile Manager, or by searching your business on Google Maps, opening the profile and copying the "Write a review" link.

name: Restaurant menu
h1: QR code for a restaurant menu
intro: Link a table-top QR code straight to your menu page (or a hosted PDF) so guests can browse without a printed menu changing hands.
tips: Host the menu at a URL you control (your own site or a PDF you own) rather than a third-party menu-builder, so the link does not depend on that company's subscription — see the PDF use case if you only have a PDF file.
Make sure the destination page is mobile-friendly; most scans happen on a phone at the table.
Laminate table cards or use a scratch-resistant sticker — a scuffed code stops scanning.
Update the linked page for daily specials instead of reprinting the code each time.

faqs.q: Will the QR code need reprinting if I change the menu?
faqs.a: No, as long as the underlying page URL stays the same — update the page's content and the same printed code keeps working.

faqs.q: Should I use a dynamic QR service so I can change the link later?
faqs.a: Only if you expect the destination URL itself to change (e.g. switching website providers). If you just update the page content, a static code to your own URL is simpler and cannot be switched off by a third party.

name: Wedding website / RSVP
h1: QR code for a wedding website or RSVP
intro: Add a QR code to invitations or signage that links guests straight to your wedding website — schedule, directions, registry and RSVP — without a long URL to type.
tips: Use the final wedding-website URL, ideally one you'll keep live well past the day for photo-sharing and thank-yous.
Pick a foreground colour that matches your stationery from the style panel, and export SVG for high-quality printing on invitations.
Add a short line of context next to the code ("Scan for details & RSVP") — guests won't scan an unexplained square.
Test the scan on both iOS and Android before the invitations go to print.

faqs.q: Which wedding-website builders work with a static code?
faqs.a: Any of them — as long as you link to the site's own URL, the QR code is independent of which builder you use and keeps working for as long as that page is live.

faqs.q: Can I use the same code for save-the-dates and invitations?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the destination URL doesn't change between the two mailings.

name: PDF document
h1: QR code for a PDF file
intro: Link a QR code to a PDF you host online (a menu, brochure, spec sheet or report) so a scan opens or downloads the document instantly.
tips: Host the PDF somewhere stable that you control (your own site, or cloud storage with a public link) — the QR code itself never expires, but only if the link keeps working.
Keep the PDF under a few MB so it opens quickly on mobile data.
Most phone browsers preview PDFs inline; there's no need for a special "PDF viewer" service.
If the file will be replaced periodically, keep the same file name/URL so the same code stays valid.

faqs.q: Can the QR code store the PDF itself?
faqs.a: No — a QR code can hold at most a couple of KB of data, far too little for a real PDF. It always links to a file hosted somewhere; make sure that hosting is reliable.

faqs.q: Does Google Drive or Dropbox work as the host?
faqs.a: Yes, using their public "share" link, though a link you fully control (your own domain) is more durable than relying on a personal cloud-storage account.

name: Calendar event
h1: QR code for a calendar event
intro: An event QR code lets a scan add the date, time and location straight into someone's calendar app — no manual entry, no missed invite.
tips: Double-check the time zone assumption: times are encoded as entered, without a time-zone offset, so make sure attendees are in the same zone or say so in the description.
Keep the title short; put full details (dress code, parking, links) in the description field.
For a recurring event, this generates a single occurrence — link to a calendar subscription instead if you need recurrence.
Print it on invitations, posters or a confirmation email footer.

faqs.q: Which calendar apps support scanning this?
faqs.a: Any calendar or camera app that understands the standard VEVENT format — this includes the built-in iOS and Android camera apps and Google Calendar's scan-to-add flow.

faqs.q: Can I update the event after printing the code?
faqs.a: Not on that same printed code — it's static. If the date or venue changes, generate and redistribute a new code.

name: PayPal.me payment link
h1: QR code for a PayPal.me link
intro: Turn your paypal.me link into a scannable QR code so customers or friends can open a pre-filled payment request without typing your username.
tips: Use your exact paypal.me/username link; add /amount at the end to pre-fill a fixed amount (e.g. paypal.me/yourname/10).
This links directly to PayPal, not through a third-party QR/payment redirect — it works for as long as your PayPal.me link is active.
Never encode card numbers, CVVs or bank details directly in a QR code; paypal.me links don't expose them, which is why they're a safer choice for print.
Put a short label next to the code ("Tip / Pay here") so the intent is unambiguous.

faqs.q: Is it safe to publish a QR code with my PayPal.me link?
faqs.a: A paypal.me link only lets someone open a payment screen to you — it cannot pull money from your account, so it's safe to post publicly, the same as sharing the link itself.

faqs.q: Can I change the amount later?
faqs.a: Generate a new code for a different fixed amount, or omit the amount from the link so payers enter it themselves.

name: Spotify track, playlist or artist
h1: QR code for a Spotify track, playlist or artist
intro: Encode an open.spotify.com link so scanning opens a track, playlist or artist page directly in the Spotify app or web player.
tips: Copy the share link from Spotify's own "Share → Copy link" menu (open.spotify.com/...) to make sure it's correct and current.
This is separate from Spotify's own built-in Scan Codes feature; ours produces a standard QR code any camera can read, styled to match your brand.
A playlist link can be updated on Spotify's side (tracks added/removed) without needing a new QR code, since the destination URL stays the same.
Great for event posters, packaging or merch — pair with an eye-catching colour from the style panel.

faqs.q: Does this work with Apple Music or other services instead?
faqs.a: Yes — use the same URL type with a music.apple.com or other streaming link; the QR code generator works with any http/https URL.

faqs.q: Will the code still work if I delete the playlist?
faqs.a: No — like any direct link, it depends on that page continuing to exist. Deleting or making the playlist private breaks the link.

name: TikTok profile
h1: QR code for your TikTok profile
intro: Link straight to your TikTok profile (tiktok.com/@yourhandle) so a scan opens your videos in the app immediately.
tips: Use the full https://tiktok.com/@yourhandle URL rather than just the handle text.
This is a direct profile link, independent of TikTok's own in-app QR/code feature, and works in any camera app.
If your handle might change, double-check it right before printing — the code cannot be edited afterwards.
Pair the code with a short call to action ("Follow us on TikTok") for context.

faqs.q: Is this the same as TikTok's in-app QR code?
faqs.a: No, but it points to the same destination. TikTok's in-app code is generated inside the app; this one is a standard QR code you can style, export as SVG/PNG and print anywhere.

faqs.q: Does it expire?
faqs.a: No — it's a direct link and only stops working if you rename or delete the profile.

name: LinkedIn profile or company page
h1: QR code for a LinkedIn profile or company page
intro: Add a QR code to a business card, resume or booth banner that links directly to your LinkedIn profile or company page.
tips: Use your public profile URL (linkedin.com/in/yourname) exactly as shown on your LinkedIn "Contact info" panel.
For a company, use the /company/ page URL rather than a personal profile if the code is meant to represent the business.
This is a direct LinkedIn link, so it keeps working as long as the profile exists at that URL — no third-party service in between.
Combine with a vCard code on the reverse of a business card for both "save contact" and "view profile" in one card — see the vCard use case.

faqs.q: Can recruiters or contacts scan this without a LinkedIn account?
faqs.a: The public profile page is viewable without logging in (with limited detail); connecting or messaging still requires an account.

faqs.q: Will this code stop working if I change my LinkedIn URL slug?
faqs.a: Yes — LinkedIn keeps redirecting old vanity URLs for a while in many cases, but it's not guaranteed. Re-generate the code if you change your custom URL.

name: Email address
h1: QR code for an email address
intro: An email QR code opens the scanner's default mail app with your address already in the "To" field — and, optionally, a pre-filled subject and message.
tips: A pre-filled subject line (e.g. "Question about…") helps you triage incoming messages at a glance.
Keep the body short; it's a starting point the sender can edit, not a locked message.
This uses the standard mailto: link, so it opens whatever mail app is set as default on the scanning device.
Good for business cards, email signatures printed on letterhead, or support desks.

faqs.q: Will this work if someone doesn't have a mail app configured?
faqs.a: If no default mail app is set, most phones will prompt to choose or set one up; a handful of browsers may show an error instead.

faqs.q: Does the QR code expose my email to spammers?
faqs.a: Anyone who decodes the image can read the address, the same as if it were printed as plain text — QR encoding does not hide or protect it.

name: Phone number
h1: QR code for a phone number
intro: A phone QR code opens the dialer with your number pre-filled — one tap to call, no typing or saving a contact first.
tips: Include the country code (e.g. +1, +44) so it dials correctly regardless of where the scanner is.
Good for "call now" signage, delivery vehicles, service stickers or classified ads.
This uses the standard tel: link, supported by every modern phone's camera app.
For a number people should save rather than just call once, use a vCard code instead.

faqs.q: Does this dial automatically when scanned?
faqs.a: No — it opens the phone's dialer with the number filled in; the person still has to tap call, so there's no risk of accidental dialing.

faqs.q: Can I include an extension?
faqs.a: Extensions aren't part of the tel: standard reliably across devices; put the base number in the code and mention the extension in nearby text instead.
